prompt: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset type: square tileable PBR diffuse/albedo texture for the broad side faces of an old Chinese elm timber bed in a realistic 3D game. Fill the entire square with ONE continuous flat old timber surface, not multiple boards. True orthographic straight overhead macro material capture covering approximately 64 by 64 centimeters. The primary grain flows left-to-right. Show convincing fine irregular interlocking elm grain and broken short pore lines, natural wavy/cathedral growth figure, a couple of small tight knots about 15-25 mm across, tiny grey-brown fibres, subtle aged finish loss and ingrained dust. Grain should have crisp organic local detail and local direction changes, not blurred elongated paint smears or uniformly straight long stripes. Weathered indoor brown-grey elm, dark old patina with occasional muted lighter brown bare wood, aged and dry rather than rotten, no orange varnish and no glossy polish. Restrained medium-dark neutral brown/grey palette, readable grain without black grooves. Uniform flat diffuse albedo illumination across the entire image, absolutely no directional highlights, no cast shadows, no large lighting gradient, no vignette. No object shape, no perspective, no plank seams, no board edges, no holes, no large cracks, no end grain rings, no lettering, no watermark, no border. All four edges should tile continuously; one full-bleed square material swatch only.
processing: Original source retained. Linear RGB periodic-plus-smooth decomposition removes repeat-edge discontinuities without spatial stretching. limitation: Artistic generated timber material, not a calibrated scan. Existing end-grain charts and real damage geometry are retained.
